subject: Performance SLO & VPC qualification — post-call recap
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-analytics.com>, Priya Singh <priya@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO & VPC qualification — post-call recap

Hi Sanjay / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on the use case and expected load. Quick recap of the perf / SLO items we agreed to validate for Redwood Private (VPC) deployment: 

- Latency targets: P50 target < 50ms, P95 target < 200ms for generation requests at steady-state.
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline 1,000 requests/sec steady; expected average concurrency ~150 active sessions, burst up to ~600.
- Streaming: we need to support server-sent streaming (chunked responses) for the interactive chat UX — low tail latency on initial token is important.
- Packet-level/internal budgets: you mentioned wanting <10ms internal app-to-egress budget inside the VPC for best UX.
- Network path: we need to validate VPN/peering configuration, egress NAT behavior, and whether traffic will hairpin through a corporate proxy.

Action items we asked for on the call (so we can run network validation tests):
1) Topology diagram (VPC subnets, NAT/IGW, Transit Gateway/Direct Connect or VPN details).
2) Public egress IP ranges or NAT gateway IPs so our SRE can whitelist.
3) A sample traceroute / packet capture from one of your app hosts to the intended Redwood egress IP.
4) Expected concurrency pattern (rps distribution, average session length, typing burst characteristics).

I've attached a simple network diagram template to show the components we usually test against. Once we have the diagram + traceroute we can schedule a joint network test (small synthetic load + streaming) and confirm p50/p95 numbers.

Proposed next steps:
- Sanjay / Priya: share topology + traceroute by EOD Tue (4/20).
- Redwood: we'll prepare firewall rules + a short test plan and propose a 60-minute window for testing next week.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network-diagram.pdf (PDF, 240KB)]

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-analytics.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya@acme-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC qualification — post-call recap

Thanks Jordan — great recap. A few answers and the attachments you requested: traceroute log attached, and I've included a simple ASCII topology below.

Short answers:
- AWS region: us-west-2 (we run our app fleet here).
- Connectivity: we plan to peer via a customer-managed VPN to Redwood's VPC (no Direct Connect initially). We also have an AWS Transit Gateway in place for connecting multiple VPCs.
- Egress: App hosts NAT via a private NAT gateway in a centralized VPC; public egress IPs are provided below.
- Concurrency: average active sessions ~150, bursts to ~600 during peak churn (we see 30-45s average typing window per session).
- Streaming: yes, streaming is required — the product uses character-level updates.
- Internal app-to-egress budget: we generally see 5-12ms internal latency between app servers and NAT/egress in the same AZ.

Public egress IPs (NAT gateways): 3.21.45.12, 3.21.45.13

Simple topology:
App Fleet (private subnets, us-west-2a/b) -> Transit GW -> Central VPC (NAT GW) -> Internet Gateway -> Redwood VPN

Attachments: traceroute-log.txt shows 6 hops to the proposed Redwood egress IP with 18-28ms median to edge; we can run tests from an app host during a maintenance window.

We'll aim to get you a cleaner diagram & a packet capture by Tuesday EOD.

Cheers,
Sanjay
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Acme Analytics

[Attachment: traceroute-log.txt (TXT, 12KB)]

Hi Sanjay — perfect, thanks for the details and the traceroute. A few immediate notes and next steps from our side: 

1) Whitelisting & firewall: our SREs will need the egress IPs you provided added to your allowlist for the inbound test connections; we'll also provide a short list of Redwood egress IPs and ports (443, 80 for health checks where needed).
2) Test plan: we'll run a 60-minute joint test that includes:
   - Synthetic streaming sessions (character-level updates) at incremental concurrency points: 150, 300, 600.
   - 5 minute steady-state at each concurrency point to capture p50/p95 and token latency.
   - A short cold-start ramp to measure first-token latency under cold KV cache.
3) Scheduling: suggest Wed 4/21 09:30-10:30 PT or Thu 4/22 13:00-14:00 PT. Which works for your infra team?
4) Deliverables from Acme: topology diagram (PDF or PPT), traceroute from one app host (pcap or traceroute output), confirmation of maintenance window and a host we can target.

Marissa — FYI on the proposed test plan above. Can you please open an internal ticket to provision a test endpoint in our private fleet (dedicated instance) and note the egress IPs we should use for the test? I'll need SRE to confirm expected capacity and whether we should enable aggressive KV pre-warming for the first-token test.

Sanjay / Priya — once you confirm the window we'll send an invite + the test-run checklist.

Thanks,
Jordan
